steps.content: With your permission, the first stop on Parfait's itinerary is an upscale gallery in Eastside.
The moment you step inside, the murmur of wealthy patrons follows you, their whispers curling through the space like smoke.

steps.speaker: Passerby A
steps.content: Isn't that Eastside's investment guru? What's she doing back here? And the person next to her is... the MBCC Chief?

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: It's about her Tulip Holdings, obviously. She has to come back for the investigation anyway. If she doesn't clean up her own mess, she's totally gonna go bankrupt.

steps.speaker: Passerby A
steps.content: Shh, she's coming over... Hello there, Parfait! Long time no see. What have you been keeping yourself busy with lately?
Parfait approaches with a bright, practiced smile. Whether she's oblivious to the gossiping whispers or just playing innocent is impossible to tell.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Oh, Richard, it truly has been too long. I've been much the same, keeping rather occupied with the development of the Outland Hypercube mine.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: I recall this Hypercube mining venture has been going on for about half a year now, hasn't it? How's the progress coming along?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Everything is going quite smoothly. If all continues as planned, I anticipate having the first shipment prepared by March of next year.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: Splendid! Once this Outland Hypercube trade route is up and running, Tulip Holdings will be absolutely gilded. Now Miss Parfait, as a personal favor to an old friend, you really must reserve me a distributor position.
His syrupy enthusiasm turns your stomach, but Parfait doesn't even blink. She shakes his hand smoothly as she replies.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Of course, I could never forget my old friends here in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: That's wonderful to hear. You have my sincerest wishes for your venture's success, and do keep me apprised of any favorable developments, won't you?

After exchanging a few more pleasantries, the two impeccably dressed patrons bid Parfait a performatively reluctant farewell, waving as they withdraw. But the instant her back turns, their expressions melt into something oddly amused.

Not that you're surprised. From the moment you and Parfait walked into this Eastside gallery, you became the center of gravity—Investment Guru Parfait, miraculously returned, and the MBCC Chief, side by side. An irresistible spectacle.
Even now, murmurs ripple through the space, eyes flicking your way constantly.

options: Who were those two just now?

choices.text: Who were those two just now?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: That man is the Executive Director of the McLenn Foundation. I've crossed paths with him at a few dinner gatherings. Strictly speaking, I suppose you could consider him a competitor of mine... After all, they have rather close ties with Nirvana.
Then why did you spend so much time talking with them?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Well, I'll admit the social etiquette in Eastside's high society can be rather tedious. Still, I do believe it's essential to uphold a certain level of decorum.
Even while talking to you, Parfait keeps smiling and offering gracious nods to acknowledge the crowd around you both.
Having to smile through all that passive-aggressiveness... That must be exhausting.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Oh, it isn't so terrible, really. Not everyone is like that. I've been fortunate to make some genuine friends here...
As she talks, her eyes light on who she's looking for in the crowd. She waves enthusiastically to a man and a woman standing nearby.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Hans, Ava?! Oh my goodness, it's been so long! ...Please excuse me for just a moment. I must pop over and say hello to my friends.
Clearly, these two must be the genuine friends Parfait mentioned. But you don't plan to wait around like she asked. You're here to watch her, after all.
However, just as you're about to follow Parfait to hear exactly what she plans to discuss with her "genuine friends," a voice calls out from behind you.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: A pleasure to meet you, Chief.
You turn, and there he is: the same man who was talking with Parfait earlier. He flashes you a beaming smile, leaning in a little too close as he strikes up conversation like you're old friends.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: You see, our dear investment guru is always like this, effortlessly gliding between celebrities and tycoons...

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: Allow me to introduce myself. I'm Richard McLenn, Executive Director of the McLenn Foundation. As far as I know, you rarely grace social gatherings such as this one. And arriving as the renowned Miss Parfait's companion... makes it all the more unusual.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: If I may be so bold as to ask, do we find ourselves graced with your presence for some particular purpose?
You resist the urge to roll your eyes. This is, after all, where Eastside's elite mingle—no sense in making enemies needlessly. So you force a perfunctory smile and explain.
I've got some confidential business to handle. Running into Parfait was just a coincidence.
Richard arches a brow, his expression knowing. He's likely already pieced together that you're here to watch Parfait. But since you shut it down first, he's too tactful to press the issue further.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: I see... Though I have to admit, I'm quite curious whether our dear investment guru will get what she's after this time.
Now that piques your interest.
You mean...?

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: The Spring Concert tickets, naturally. It's the premier social event of the season that virtually all of Eastside's elite will attend. This would be such a convenient opportunity for Miss Parfait to... reacquaint herself with old friends she hasn't seen in ages. Unfortunately...
Unfortunately?

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: Unfortunately, VIP seats are impossible to come by these days. Tulip Holdings is mired in crisis, and the investment guru herself is drowning in scandal. Well... let's just say she shouldn't expect many warm welcomes. I do fear she'll find herself leaving empty-handed.
Seeing that his words have piqued your interest, Richard continues in a lowered voice.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: I'm sure you're aware of Parfait's questionable background. In her early years, she was quite inseparable from certain Syndican circles, and even during recent years, she's been using her so-called "Parfait's Dinner Party" as an excuse to bring all sorts of suspicious characters into establishments far above their usual standing.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: The Eastside consensus these days is that Tulip Holdings' remarkable financial reports in its early years were... shall we say, purely due to her shady dealings with Syndicate gangsters. Money laundering, if we're being blunt.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: How fortunate, then, that your decisive interventions completely restructured those organizations. Syndicate has entered a new era, and that, quite coincidentally, severed her original revenue streams. That's why she announced her plans to "develop an Outland Hypercube mine" six months ago.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: A shame, of course. The investment guru's golden reputation is now completely tarnished. And once panic selling begins? Well. No fund, no matter how pristine, survives a full-blown stampede.
You have no interest in this tedious mix of slander and flattery, offering noncommittal hums and nods while stealing glances at Parfait, who is deep in animated conversation with her two friends.
But the man's too wrapped up in his own enthusiasm to notice your half-hearted responses, riding high on whatever point he's trying to make.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: Any real businessman can spot that Outland Hypercube mine of hers for the folly it is. Meanwhile, our West District operations have already begun actual extraction. Naturally, we Eastside investors have been... keen to participate. Yet somehow, Rustfire maintains such exclusive control, and we've never found a way in...

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: Chief, given your... exceptional rapport with the West District, we were hoping you might facilitate an introduction... Consider it our way of contributing to our sister district's reconstruction efforts.

The second he says it, you almost snap. Another Eastside opportunist eyeing the West District's Hypercube mining, just like the dozens before him. Every last one has been a vulture, circling for profit, never lifting a finger unless there's something in it for them. You've grown so sick of it.
Eager to get over to Parfait's side, you offer a perfunctory response.
This could be tough to set up. I'll ask around, but I can't promise anything concrete.

steps.speaker: Richard
steps.content: I'll be counting on you, then. By the way, Spring Concert VIP tickets are quite hard to come by, but I happen to have some connections in that circle. Would you like me to have someone send a few your way...
Without waiting for Richard to respond, you wave your hand dismissively.
I have to go now. Excuse me.
You escape Richard's attention and weave through the gallery, taking the long way around before finally approaching Parfait's group.
As you arrive, the young man among them continues chatting with infectious enthusiasm, his excitement and joy appearing completely genuine.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: ...And then I met the artist himself in the auction house's VIP room. You'll never believe this: the genius behind that masterpiece is barely twenty years old, just some ordinary Syndicate kid like any other street rat you'd pass without noticing.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Hans, you know what I always say. Art doesn't care where you come from. Real talent and beautiful virtues can shine through in anyone, no matter their background.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Come now, I couldn't disagree more. How many generations does it take Syndicate to produce a talent like this? And let's be honest, without connoisseurs like ourselves to recognize his worth, those Syndicate paupers would probably be selling his masterpieces as wrapping paper...

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Honestly, you two... Must you argue about this every time? You're giving me such a headache...
The elegantly dressed woman beside them interrupts Hans and Parfait's endless debate.

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Parfait, I was so sorry to hear about your partner's disappearance and those dreadful debts. How is Tulip Holdings faring?

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Just rest assured, Ava. This is Parfait we're talking about—the so-called investment guru for good reason. When have you ever seen her fail?Business ups and downs are always temporary...

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: You should know both the Financial Inspection Team and Nirvana have Parfait under close watch now. And I've heard that your uncle's been spreading rumors to depress Tulip's stock while quietly accumulating shares on the secondary market... At this rate, they might completely edge Parfait out.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Don't worry about me.
Faced with her deeply concerned friend, Parfait maintains her characteristic confidence.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: This stage does need some tactical adjustments, but I've already mapped out all the next steps for the business strategy. Once next quarter's financials are out, the pressure should ease on its own.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But let's not dwell on that now. Ava, any updates on those tickets I mentioned?

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Of course I wouldn't forget.
Ava reaches into her handbag and produces a black matte ticket bordered in gold before handing it over to Parfait.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Holy ****, a VIP ticket?! a VIP ticket?! How on earth did you score one this late?

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: It's from my father.
For a moment, you catch a flash of shock and embarrassment on Parfait's face that she fails to hide.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I... I really shouldn't take this.

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Why not? You know these events aren't really my sort of thing. After last month's breakup, I'm hardly in concert-going spirits anyway. Father practically insisted I take it. If you hadn't returned, I likely would've passed it along as a favor to someone else.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Oh? Since when have you disliked these events?

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Oh, quiet you! This is a prime seat. You'll be right next to Sheffield from the Financial Inspection Team, Prosecutor Eddie, and my father...

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Well, I'll be damned, Parfait, this ticket is practically tailor-made for you.Her old man's the primary investor behind Tulip Holdings, isn't he? You two really should have a proper chat.
Parfait's gaze flickers anxiously, her words tripping over themselves.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Oh, but that's... that's not quite... what we agreed on. We said regular tickets would be fine. And actually, I was hoping to bring a few friends along. Just one ticket wouldn't be enough...

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Enough about the regular tickets. When you were on top, you could parade your dodgy entourage through the cheap seats and they'd still hail you as the investment guru for being unconventional. But this isn't the time for stubbornness.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Look at these absurd rumors circulating about you now—"Tulip Holdings involved with illegal Syndicate operations?" Tch, half of Eastside can't claim clean hands themselves...

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: But to call you some Syndicate con artist, always lurking in the slums? That's what truly disgusts me. The sheer lack of thought, as if someone of your caliber could ever be mistaken for their gutter trash.
The smooth-talking socialite you've been watching finally drops his carefree act. His playful expression fades as he gazes at Parfait, his voice uncharacteristically earnest.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Listen, Parfait, whatever people are saying out there, we believe in you. Ava, me, all of your friends. That's not changing. You're not getting through this crisis alone. Count on that.

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Exactly. Your first priority now is maintaining calm with both the Financial Inspection Team and Nirvana, while reassuring investors and partners. Which is precisely why you need this ticket more than anyone else.
Ava presses the ticket firmly into Parfait's hand.

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Oh, by the way, Hans and I have a dinner engagement later with Sheffield and his group. Would you like to join us?
Parfait falls silent, the VIP ticket clutched in her hand as she offers a bitter smile. Having noticed your arrival since a while ago, she glances instinctively in your direction.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Oh, no thank you... but I'll have to pass for now.
Her two friends turn to look at you in unison. The warm concern they have shown Parfait melts into perfectly practiced smiles. Hans even inclines his head in a polite greeting.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Well then, we won't keep you any longer. See you at the concert.
As they pass by, you catch Hans murmuring to Ava in a hushed voice.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: See, stop worrying. She's even got the MBCC Chief on her side now. Parfait is more resourceful than we gave her credit for...
You watch the two wealthy young people walk away until they disappear from view, then finally approach Parfait.
Hey, what's going on? You've got your ticket, but you still look pretty down.
Parfait's face is etched with bitterness.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But I... from the very beginning, I wanted to bring my friends along with me.
She holds up the gleaming gilded concert ticket, furrowing her brow as she lets out a long sigh.

steps.speaker: jojo
steps.content: No matter how amazing a VIP ticket is, it can't fit more than ten people...
...More than ten people?
Parfait stands frozen in place, silent for a long while. Her fingers twist absently through her hair, disheveling what had been a carefully styled arrangement.
I could help?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But how? At this point... even regular tickets are impossible to come by...
That Richard you just spoke with came by earlier, trying to give me some tickets.
He looks pretty gullible. Want me to go ask him for you?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Really?!
Parfait's head jerks up, her eyes lighting up for just a second before she catches herself. The hope vanishes as she narrows her eyes, leaning back with new suspicion.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Wait, what do you want in return?
You know how it is in my line of work. We're a naturally curious bunch. And I have to say, I'm particularly interested in these "more than ten friends" you're planning to invite.
How about this: you share who they are, and I'll help you out. Sounds good?
The moment those words leave your mouth, Parfait's expectant expression shatters, suspicion flooding in to take its place.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Then... then please don't trouble yourself over this. I'll figure something out on my own...
